gist: Sabrina Bahsoon experienced sudden psychotic symptoms initially misdiagnosed as stress and lack of sleep.

Bahsoon is now recovering in Malaysia and hopes to raise awareness of the rare disease.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Content creator Sabrina Bahsoon began experiencing erratic behaviour and psychotic symptoms in March. After being discharged from A&E with sleeping tablets, police brought her to hospital where she was sectioned and treated with antipsychotic medication. Two months later, she was diagnosed with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis caused by ovarian tumours, and had surgery in June.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Bahsoon wants to raise awareness of the rare autoimmune disease and encourage people to advocate for their treatment. An NHS trust apologised after an internal review found initial assessment aspects were not followed up properly.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The first Children's Booker prize revealed its shortlist and the children chosen to judge the books. A panel of child judges, along with adults including Frank Cottrell-Boyce, Lolly Adefope and Sanchita Basu De Sarkar, will determine the winner. The announcement of the victorious book is scheduled for February next year at the Young V and A in London, accompanied by the distribution of 30,000 copies to children in need.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The prize aims to address concerning statistics regarding declining reading enjoyment among children and young people. By including children on the judging panel, the organisers ensure that young readers have a direct and powerful voice in deciding which book deserves to win.
